chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ibn Fazzal from Mansur ibn Yunus from Abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said:

The believer is silent to be safe, and speaks to benefit. He neither discusses his entrustments with the friends nor does he conceal his testimony from the remote ones, nor does he do anything of the goodness for showing off, nor does he neglect it due to bashfulness. If he is praised, he fears what they might be saying, and he seeks Forgiveness of Allah for what they do not know. The words of the ignorant one do not deceive him, and he fears the counting of what he has done.
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical characteristics and behaviors of a true believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) defines the believer's character through the discipline of speech, distinguishing between protective silence and purposeful speech. It further elaborates on the psychological state of the faithful, who remain humble before public opinion yet vigilant against divine accountability, ensuring their deeds are sincere rather than driven by vanity or modesty.
